description: Synthetic Orders SDK corpus; measures retrieval, not model or customer application quality.

documents.content:
# Authenticate an order status request

For Orders SDK 1.2.3, load ORDERS_API_KEY from the customer's server environment. Set Authorization: Bearer using that application credential. Call GET /v1/orders/{order_id}. A successful response has status 200 and an order status. Treat 401 as an invalid application credential; do not retry it and do not use a DokoSoko access token as the vendor API key.

# List every order using cursor pagination

Call GET /v1/orders?limit=20. Append each page's items in order. When next_cursor is nonempty, pass it unchanged as the cursor query parameter. Stop when next_cursor is empty. Reject a repeated cursor and cap the request count at 100 so a broken upstream cannot create an infinite pagination loop.

# Recover from a rate limit

For a read request returning HTTP 429, honor Retry-After seconds before retrying. Cap retries at two additional attempts, keep the same request, and stop on success. Reject a Retry-After delay above 30 seconds instead of waiting indefinitely. Do not retry HTTP 401 or non-idempotent writes automatically.

# Create an order without duplicates

Send POST /v1/orders with an Idempotency-Key unique to one logical order creation. If the response is lost, retry with the same key and the same JSON payload. The server returns the original order ID without creating a second order. Reusing the key with a different payload must return HTTP 409. Never generate a new key merely because a response was lost.

# Verify the webhook signature before parsing JSON

For Orders SDK 1.2.3, read the unchanged raw request body. The X-Orders-Signature header is lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + '.' + raw body, keyed with the webhook signing secret. Read the timestamp from X-Orders-Timestamp. Compare decoded signature bytes in constant time. Reject an invalid signature before parsing JSON or running the order handler.

# Reject stale webhook timestamps and duplicate events

After webhook signature validation, require the X-Orders-Timestamp to be within 300 seconds of the server clock, including future timestamps. Parse the event only after signature and timestamp checks. Deduplicate accepted events by event_id before triggering the order handler. A duplicate valid event returns HTTP 200 without repeating the side effect; an expired or altered event returns HTTP 400.

# Change dashboard appearance

Choose a dashboard color theme, upload a team avatar, and reorder saved reports. These controls change the vendor dashboard appearance; they do not configure authentication for an application.

# Export billing reports

Request a CSV billing report in the account dashboard. Reports include invoice totals and currency codes. Download links expire after one day.

# Configure shipping addresses

Collect a delivery address and parcel dimensions at checkout. Shipping zones determine delivery methods. Postal code formatting depends on the destination country.

# Search order history

Filter existing order history by creation date and customer reference. Search results are read-only and do not create or cancel an order.

# Configure email notifications

Select a sender display name and a notification template. Preview translated messages in the dashboard before enabling the email delivery schedule.

# Configure report retention

Archived reports are retained for 90 days. Export required records before the retention window ends. Deleting an archived report does not cancel an order.
